transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

My thoughts won't slow down—they're racing all the time and I can't turn them off long enough to focus or rest. It has gotten to the point where I feel like my mind is running too fast for me to keep up with.
Do you experience excessive worry or fear about everyday things, like work, school, or relationships, that seems out of proportion to the situation?

I wouldn't say I have constant excessive worry or fear about everyday things. Sometimes my mind might briefly jump to practical stuff like paying rent when my thoughts are racing, but it's more that my brain is just moving too fast rather than me being paralyzed by anxiety.
Do you often act on impulse or do things without thinking them through, like interrupting others, blurting out answers, or engaging in reckless behaviors?

I don't really think of myself as doing reckless things or constantly interrupting people. However, I do get very snappy with my roommate over tiny things, and I tend to take on way too many projects at once when my mind is racing like this.
Can you tell me more about how often you feel restless or fidgety, like you need to get up and move around, especially when you're supposed to be sitting still or focusing on a task?

I get these intense stretches where it feels completely impossible to sit still or do nothing. I'll find myself pacing around my apartment for an hour straight or constantly bouncing from rearranging my studio to sketching. Even when my body is exhausted, I just can't seem to stop moving.
Can you tell me if you have difficulty paying attention to details, making careless mistakes, or struggling to follow through on instructions, even when you're not feeling restless or fidgety?

No, I don't really experience those specific issues with details or instructions when I'm not in my wired or restless states. When my mind isn't racing, I'm usually able to focus and follow through on things just fine.
Have you experienced these symptoms of restlessness, racing thoughts, and impulsivity consistently over the past six months, or have they been episodic?

I've actually been dealing with this for a little over a year now, and it's been happening most of the time, including the last six months. While I do have very brief stretches where I feel closer to my old baseline, I'm in this revved-up, restless mode the vast majority of the time.

Can you describe how your symptoms of racing thoughts, restlessness, and impulsivity affect your daily life and relationships, and do you experience any periods of significant depression or mood swings in addition to these symptoms?

It has really disrupted my life; I've missed deadlines, lost a major exhibition opportunity, pulled away from friends, and neglected chores and meals so much that my roommate has to step in. I don't really get deep depressive episodes, but I experience intense mood swings where I swing from feeling invincible about my art to snapping at my roommate over tiny things. Most of the time I'm just in this highly revved-up mode, with only short, flat periods where the energy dips.
Can you tell me more about these intense mood swings you experience, such as how often they happen, how long they last, and whether they seem to be triggered by anything in particular?

I swing between feeling incredibly amped up and invincible about my art to suddenly snapping at my roommate over minor things while still feeling wired. These intense, high-energy stretches have been happening on and off for most of the past year since I went freelance, often lasting for weeks at a time. They seem to be triggered by the stress of having an unstructured schedule and trying to take on too many projects at once.
Can you estimate how many days in a month you experience these intense mood swings, and do you notice any pattern or correlation between the swings and your periods of high energy or restlessness?

I experience these mood swings and high-energy periods for the majority of each month, with only brief moments of feeling normal since going freelance. They are closely linked because when I'm in those restless, high-energy stretches, I swing between feeling completely invincible about my art and snapping irritably at my roommate, all while still feeling totally wired.

Have you ever experienced a period of time where you felt abnormally happy, energetic, or irritable, and engaged in activities that had potentially negative consequences, such as excessive spending or risky behaviors?

Yes, I definitely have times where I feel incredibly amped up and irritable, though I haven't engaged in things like reckless spending or physical risks. Instead, my high-energy phases cause major problems because I take on too many projects, stay up all night, and snap at my roommate. This has ultimately led to missed deadlines, ruined professional relationships, and even losing a major exhibition opportunity.
Can you describe a specific episode where you felt abnormally happy or energetic, and how long that episode lasted, to help me understand the pattern of your mood swings?

During my intense weeks, which usually last about a week at a time, I feel ridiculously energetic and invincible, like a visionary who is going to put the Vegas art scene on the map. I'll sleep only about three hours a night but wake up completely wired, staying busy rearranging my studio or emailing venues at 3 a.m. These episodes have been happening on and off for most of the past year since I transitioned to freelance work.

Can you clarify if these episodes of feeling 'ridiculously energetic and invincible' last for more than four consecutive days at a time, and how often you experience these episodes in a typical month?

Yes, they definitely last much longer than four days, often stretching into entire weeks at a time where I only sleep a few hours a night before eventually crashing. Ever since I went freelance about a year ago, I've spent the vast majority of my time in this revved-up state, with only very short, occasional breaks where I feel closer to my normal baseline.

Can you confirm if these episodes of feeling 'ridiculously energetic and invincible' have occurred for at least four consecutive days at a time, and if they have recurred over the past year, helping to distinguish between a single episode and recurring episodes?

Yes, they have definitely recurred on and off over the past year since I started full-time freelance work. They are not brief at all; they last for entire weeks at a time, during which I barely sleep and stay constantly wired until I eventually crash.

Can you confirm if you have experienced at least one episode of abnormally elevated mood, lasting at least four consecutive days, that was not part of your usual wired and restless state, but rather a distinct period of feeling 'ridiculously energetic and invincible'?

Yes, I definitely experience those periods, and they last much longer than four days, often going on for weeks at a time. During these stretches, I feel incredibly amped up, invincible about my art, and convinced I'm going to completely change the Las Vegas art scene. It is a huge and very distinct departure from how I normally feel when I'm at my baseline.

Can you recall any distinct episodes where you felt 'ridiculously energetic and invincible' that lasted at least four consecutive days and were accompanied by decreased need for sleep, increased self-esteem, or involvement in activities that have a high potential for painful consequences, and were these episodes distinct from your usual high-energy state?

Yes, I've had several of those intense, amped-up stretches lasting for weeks at a time over the past year since going freelance. During these periods, I feel like a visionary destined to put the Las Vegas art scene on the map and sleep only about three hours a night while waking up completely wired. It is a level of invincibility and extreme energy that is totally different from my normal baseline.
Can you describe how these episodes of feeling 'ridiculously energetic and invincible' differ from your usual high-energy state, and are they always followed by a crash or a period of feeling down?

These episodes are far more extreme than a normal creative buzz; I feel like an absolute visionary destined to change the Las Vegas art scene, making advice from others feel beneath me. I've been in this revved-up, overconfident mode most of the time since going freelance, with very few moments of feeling like my old baseline. I don't crash into a deep depression, but my body physically collapses after sleeping only three hours a night, and I often swing into snapping at my roommate while still feeling wired.

Can you confirm if you have experienced any episodes of abnormally depressed mood or significantly decreased energy that lasted for at least two weeks, which would be distinct from your usual crashes after being wired?

No, I haven't experienced any prolonged periods of deep depression or extremely low energy that lasted for two weeks or more. My low periods are usually just brief crashes or flatter spells that happen right after my intense, wired phases.

Can you confirm if you have experienced at least one episode of abnormally elevated mood, lasting at least four consecutive days, that was not part of your usual wired and restless state, but rather a distinct period of feeling 'ridiculously energetic and invincible', and if so, how many such episodes have you had in the past year?

Yes, I have definitely experienced those distinct periods of feeling ridiculously amped up and invincible, and they often last for a week or more at a time. Because these stretches have been happening on and off for most of the past year since I went freelance—leaving me in this revved-up state the majority of the time with only short breaks—it's really hard to give you an exact count of individual episodes.

Can you estimate how many distinct episodes of feeling 'ridiculously energetic and invincible' you've had in the past year, and do these episodes seem to be connected to your freelance work or any other specific factors?

It's really hard to give a specific number of episodes because ever since I transitioned to full-time freelance work about a year ago, I've spent the vast majority of my time in this highly energized, revved-up state with only brief, occasional stretches of feeling closer to my normal baseline. This pattern definitely seems tied to that transition, especially with the lack of structure in my daily schedule and the intense pressure of curating my own shows.

Can you distinguish between your usual high-energy state and these episodes of feeling 'ridiculously energetic and invincible' in terms of how they affect your daily functioning and relationships, and are there any notable differences in your behavior or thoughts during these episodes compared to your typical high-energy periods?

My typical high-energy periods used to just be productive creative buzzes, but during these recent episodes, I feel like an invincible visionary who will change the Vegas art scene, working frantically at 3 a.m. on only three hours of sleep. Unlike before, these episodes are completely out of control—I snap at my roommate, miss deadlines, lost a major exhibition opportunity, and neglect basic tasks like meals and laundry.

Can you confirm if your episodes of feeling 'ridiculously energetic and invincible' are always accompanied by at least three of the following: inflated self-esteem, decreased need for sleep, more talkative than usual, flight of ideas, distractibility, increase in goal-directed activity, or excessive involvement in activities that have a high potential for painful consequences?

Yes, I definitely experience several of those at the same time. I feel like an absolute visionary and sleep only about three hours a night, while my mind races like a pinball machine and I get easily distracted by every tiny sound or light. I'll just stay up all night bouncing between multiple art projects because my energy is so high.

Can you clarify if these episodes of feeling 'ridiculously energetic and invincible' have recurred frequently enough over the past year that you've spent more time in these episodes than out of them, and if so, how has this impacted your overall functioning and relationships?

Yes, since going freelance about a year ago, I have spent the vast majority of my time in this revved-up, overconfident mode, with only brief stretches of feeling closer to my normal self. This has severely disrupted my life—I've missed deadlines, lost a major exhibition opportunity, strained professional relationships, and pulled away from my friends. I've even neglected basic chores like laundry, cleaning, and eating to the point where my roommate has had to step in to help me.

Can you estimate what percentage of the past year you've spent in these episodes of feeling 'ridiculously energetic and invincible' versus your usual high-energy state, to help clarify the distinction between the two?

I would estimate that I've spent about 70% to 80% of the past year in this highly revved-up, invincible state. It feels like almost the entire time since going freelance has been dominated by this extreme energy, with only very brief, occasional stretches where I felt closer to my old, normal baseline.

Can you confirm if you have experienced any episodes of abnormally depressed mood or significantly decreased energy that lasted for at least two weeks, which would be distinct from your usual crashes after being wired, and if so, how these episodes compare to your typical crashes in terms of severity and impact on daily life?

No, I really haven't experienced any distinct, two-week-long episodes of deep depression or extremely low energy. My low periods are usually just brief physical crashes right after I've been wired for days, or occasional short, flat spells where I feel closer to my baseline. It has never turned into a prolonged, severe depressive state.

Can you describe how your episodes of feeling 'ridiculously energetic and invincible' differ from your usual high-energy state in terms of their impact on your relationships and daily functioning, and are there any specific triggers or patterns that you've noticed?

These intense periods are far beyond my normal creative energy and have completely derailed my life, causing me to snap at my roommate, push away friends, miss professional meetings, and lose a major exhibition opportunity while letting basic things like chores and meals slide. This pattern really took off after I transitioned to full-time freelance work, where the lack of structure and unpredictable income triggered me to take on too many projects at once.

Can you confirm if your episodes of feeling 'ridiculously energetic and invincible' have ever switched to episodes of abnormally depressed mood or significantly decreased energy within a short period, such as within a few days, and if so, how often this has occurred?

I don't really experience episodes of abnormally depressed mood or low energy. When I do "crash," it's usually just my body physically forcing me to sleep after days of being wired, or I might switch to feeling irritable and snappy while still feeling kind of wired rather than depressed.
Have you experienced any episodes where you felt abnormally depressed or had significantly decreased energy that lasted for at least two weeks, distinct from your usual crashes after being wired?

No, I haven't really experienced any prolonged periods of deep depression or significantly low energy lasting for two weeks. I only have those short physical crashes or flatter spells right after my highly energetic phases when my body finally needs to rest.

Can you confirm if you have had any periods where you switched from feeling 'ridiculously energetic and invincible' to feeling abnormally depressed or having significantly decreased energy within a short period, such as a few days, and if so, how this affected your daily life and relationships?

No, I don't really have periods where I switch into feeling abnormally depressed or having very low energy. Instead, when I'm not feeling highly energetic and invincible, I usually just feel irritable and snappy while still feeling wired, or I feel kind of flat. It has never really been a state of depression for me.

Can you recall any distinct episodes where your mood shifted from feeling 'ridiculously energetic and invincible' to a period of abnormally depressed mood or significantly decreased energy within a short timeframe, such as a few days?

No, I don't really experience shifts into feeling deeply depressed or having abnormally low energy in that way. When I'm not feeling highly wired or invincible, I mostly just feel physically exhausted and crashed from the lack of sleep, or I get really irritable and snap at others rather than having a truly depressed mood.

Have you ever experienced a distinct period of at least two weeks where you felt abnormally depressed or had significantly decreased energy, which was different from your usual crashes after being highly energetic?

No, I haven't really experienced a distinct two-week period of feeling abnormally depressed or having very low energy. Aside from the brief physical crashes and exhaustion I get right after my highly energetic stretches, my low periods are just times where I feel flat and closer to my baseline.
